````
The extension does not receive the Resend API key or raw reply tokens. Its stdout is reserved for the Copilot JSON-RPC transport, so diagnostics go through the extension logging API or stderr. It logs a short request ID, sanitized outbound content, and every injected email prompt into the visible Copilot timeline, never the reply-to address, token, PIN, or permission reply.

### Local daemon

The daemon is the single owner of mutable state and the Resend client.

Responsibilities:

- send question, failure, and completion emails;
- poll Resend's received-email list and retrieve new message bodies;
- correlate replies using an opaque token in the reply-to address;
- resolve a native question, native permission, or agent-tool request, or enqueue a new session prompt;
- deliver at most one reply at a time to each connected extension;
- suppress duplicate events and inbound messages;
- own the away-mode flag, away PIN, notification caps, and STOP state;
- persist a small amount of routing state to survive a restart.

The `amail away`, `amail answer`, and `amail stop` commands are thin authenticated clients of the daemon. They never write the state file directly; the daemon is the sole writer.

For the take-home, the daemon owns one atomically replaced JSON state file under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\amail\`. Only routing metadata is persisted:

```text
sessions: session ID, cwd, bridge connection ID, away/stopped state, PIN hash, notification counters
requests: request ID, session ID, kind, token hash, request hash, status, expiry
queuedFollowups: session ID, cleaned prompt (4 KB maximum), status, expiry, originating idle marker
seenInbound: Resend message ID and timestamp
```

Full emails are not persisted. Only an accepted, cleaned follow-up prompt may be stored, capped at 4 KB and deleted after delivery or expiry. State-file access is restricted to the current Windows user.

The daemon generates a random pipe name and handshake secret at startup and stores them beneath `%LOCALAPPDATA%\amail\`, relying on the Windows profile's default ACL. The pipe uses an exclusive listener and a nonce/HMAC challenge; neither side sends the secret in cleartext. Processes running as the same Windows user remain inside the accepted MVP trust boundary.

The daemon creates its state directory before atomic writes so temporary files inherit the same profile ACL. It is the sole writer and uses write-temporary, flush, and rename with bounded retry. Corrupt state is backed up; all outstanding capabilities are invalidated before starting clean.

The daemon may restart independently. If the extension disconnects, accepted follow-up instructions remain queued. Native request IDs and pending tool callbacks are not durable; their tokens are expired on disconnect. A reconnect with a different session ID disarms away mode, rotates the PIN, discards old-session follow-ups, and sends a local warning. The daemon must not start a competing `--resume` process.

### Resend integration

Outbound mail uses the existing `RESEND_API_KEY` from `../.env`.

Inbound mail uses a Resend-managed receiving domain for setup speed. The daemon polls the Received Emails API every few seconds, then retrieves the full plain-text body for unseen messages. This avoids requiring a public webhook during the demo; a webhook can replace polling without changing the routing model.

Each message uses a reply-to address such as:

```text
reply+<opaque-token>@<resend-managed-domain>
```

Tokens use at least 128 random bits encoded as lowercase base32. Each token is single-use and scoped to one request kind: native question, explicit tool request, permission, or follow-up. Native-question tokens expire after 2 hours, tool waits after 30 minutes, permission tokens after 30 minutes, and follow-ups after 24 hours. A question or permission token can never become a general follow-up prompt.

Routing and authorization depend on the capability token and exact parsed sender address rather than subject text. `In-Reply-To` and `References` are recorded when available for diagnostics and threading, but missing thread headers do not reject an otherwise valid reply. Outbound mail sets `Auto-Submitted: auto-generated`. Inbound auto-replies and list mail are rejected.

If Resend exposes SPF, DKIM, or DMARC results through received headers, failed authentication is rejected. A failed or unavailable authentication result cannot approve permissions without the local away PIN.

Before delivery, the daemon caps raw message size, decodes transfer encoding, requires exactly one parsed `From` address, rejects bounces and empty or HTML-only bodies, normalizes Unicode, removes zero-width characters, strips quoted history and signatures, and caps cleaned content at 4 KB. Common forwarded-message markers produce a best-effort warning rather than authorization.

For permission replies, everything after the first line is discarded. The away PIN has at least 40 random bits, is stored only as a hash, rotates on `away off`, daemon restart, session replacement, or three failed attempts, and is never logged, persisted in plaintext, or echoed in rejection mail.

Message content and routing tokens transit Resend and may be visible in its dashboard; this is disclosed in the README. A compromised authorized mailbox is outside the MVP threat model.

## State machine

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    direction LR

    [*] --> Idle

    Idle --> Running: terminal prompt
    Idle --> FollowupQueued: authorized follow-up email
    FollowupQueued --> DeliveryAccepted: session.send accepts
    DeliveryAccepted --> Running: matching root user.message
    FollowupQueued --> Idle: session.send rejects

    Running --> WaitingForNativeAnswer: user_input.requested
    WaitingForNativeAnswer --> Running: terminal or email wins CAS
    WaitingForNativeAnswer --> TerminalOnly: email expires or bridge disconnects
    TerminalOnly --> Running: terminal answers
    WaitingForNativeAnswer --> Interrupted: root turn aborts

    Running --> WaitingForToolAnswer: ask_human_by_email
    WaitingForToolAnswer --> Running: authorized answer
    WaitingForToolAnswer --> Interrupted: timeout, abort, or disconnect

    Running --> WaitingForPermission: permission.requested
    WaitingForPermission --> Running: terminal, policy, APPROVE, or DENY
    WaitingForPermission --> TerminalOnly: email expires or bridge disconnects
    WaitingForPermission --> Interrupted: root turn aborts

    Running --> Idle: root session.idle
    Running --> Interrupted: aborted root session.idle
    Interrupted --> Idle: interruption email recorded

    Idle --> SessionEnded: CLI exits
    Running --> SessionEnded: CLI exits
    SessionEnded --> [*]
```

Away mode is an independent guard on outbound email transitions; when it is off, native questions and permissions remain entirely in the TUI.

Only one `session.send()` call may be outstanding per session. Before injection, the daemon verifies that the session has remained continuously idle since the completion email's idle marker; otherwise it rejects the stale follow-up with a notice. The cleaned prompt is persisted before `session.send()`. Once `session.send()` reports acceptance, `amail` never retries it automatically, even if the later root `user.message` confirmation is missed. Confirmation uses the typed send result plus a single outstanding delivery and exact content hash.

Injected turns set `displayPrompt` to identify the originating completion email and timestamp in the TUI.

## Alternatives considered

| Approach | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Replace native `ask_user` handler | Reject | It displaces the TUI and makes email failure block the only responder. |
| Observe and resolve native questions | Choose | Copilot's request ID and atomic `success` result preserve the TUI and make first-responder-wins safe. |
| Config hooks only | Reject | Hooks can notify or make an immediate decision, but cannot durably return an email answer hours later. |
| Start `copilot --resume` beside the open CLI | Reject | Concurrent access has no session locking and can create competing owners with stale or interleaved state. |
| ACP client | Reject for this MVP | ACP can own or restore a session, but cannot attach to the existing TUI process. |
| `/remote` | Useful fallback | It controls the live CLI through GitHub web/mobile, but exposes no supported custom email-service API. |
| ConPTY/`node-pty` wrapper | Reject unless extensions fail | It preserves the TUI and permits input injection, but adds terminal-hosting and screen-stream complexity that the extension API avoids. |
| Foreground CLI extension | Choose | It joins the exact interactive session and exposes native request events, structured RPC responses, tools, and `session.send()`. |

## Trust and safety boundaries

- Accept inbound instructions only from the configured email address.
- Use high-entropy, single-use, kind-scoped routing tokens and store only SHA-256 hashes.
- Consume a pending token atomically before acting on its reply.
- Treat email bodies as untrusted input, never as shell syntax or CLI flags.
- Deliver replies only through native request-resolution RPC, the agent tool result, or `session.send()`; never construct a shell command from a reply.
- Do not include environment variables, raw transcripts, tool outputs, or stack traces in outgoing mail.
- Redact common credential patterns before truncating the latest root assistant response.
- Apply the same redaction and 4 KB cap to permission/error payloads and model-supplied tool subjects, questions, and context.
- Ignore attachments in the MVP.
- Record Resend message IDs to make inbound processing idempotent.
- Reject auto-responders and list mail. Treat forwarded-content detection as a best-effort warning, not an authorization control.
- Authenticate a random Windows pipe name with a separate 128-bit handshake secret stored under the user's `%LOCALAPPDATA%` profile.
- Keep `RESEND_API_KEY` in the daemon; do not request or pass it into the extension process.
- Read only `RESEND_API_KEY` from the explicitly configured `../.env`; do not load or pass through unrelated variables, export it into the shell that launches Copilot, or log the key.
- Acknowledge that the Resend key can read received mail for the configured receiving domain and rotate it after the exercise.
- Require away mode for automatic native-question, permission, error, and completion emails.
- `away off` stops new notifications, expires outstanding native-question and permission tokens, rotates the PIN, and leaves standalone follow-ups untouched.
- Restrict email permission decisions to `approve-once`, bind them to a hash of the exact permission request, and require the local away PIN.
- Accept fail-safe `STOP` from the configured sender at any amail reply address even when its token is expired or unknown. `STOP THIS` scopes it to the addressed session; plain `STOP` is global.
- Persist STOP state, expire outstanding question/tool tokens, reject pending permissions, and require a local command to re-arm.
- Enforce one global budget across all outbound kinds: 20 messages per hour and 60 per day, plus at most one error email per session per 10 minutes.
- On budget exhaustion, send one final coalesced notice, suppress further mail, and require local re-arming.
- Cap agent-tool email requests at five per session, deduplicate identical content, and cap email-injected follow-up turns at five per session.

## Failure behavior

- Resend send failure: persist the notification and retry with bounded backoff; surface the failure in the local CLI.
- Inbound polling failure: keep the Copilot request waiting and show daemon health locally.
- Unknown, expired, superseded, or race-losing reply: do not route it; send one rate-limited rejection notice without a new capability token.
- Duplicate reply: acknowledge only the first delivery with that Resend message ID.
- Copilot still running a turn: use `session.send()` in its default enqueue mode rather than implementing another queue in the extension.
- Native question completed by the TUI: expire its email token on `user_input.completed`.
- Native email answer loses the compare-and-set: reject it and never fall back to `session.send()`.
- Choice-only native answer does not match an option: leave the TUI request pending and email the valid choices again.
- Agent-tool wait reaches its configurable 30-minute timeout, external-tool completion, aborted root idle, or shutdown: resolve it with an explicit no-answer result and expire its token.
- Locally present user wants to answer an explicit tool request: `amail answer <text>` resolves it through the daemon without email.
- Permission completed by the TUI or policy: expire its token on `permission.completed`.
- Extension reload: expire native and tool request tokens because their ephemeral runtime state cannot be reconstructed; keep only standalone follow-up instructions queued for the matching session.
- CLI exit: keep the reply queued, but require the user to resume an interactive session; do not start a competing Copilot process automatically.
- Daemon restart: restore routing metadata, continue polling from persisted message IDs, and let the extension reconnect.
- Root idle with `aborted: true`: send an "Interrupted" message, never a "Complete" message.
- Root idle without an assistant message: send a minimal status email rather than remaining silent.
- Sub-agent questions and permissions: mirror them with an agent label; ignore sub-agent events only for completion summaries.
- Autopilot mode: do not offer email question handling because Copilot may auto-answer user-input requests.
- Extension shutdown cleanup is driven by session events and pipe closure, not Windows signal handling.
- Prune `seenInbound` entries after seven days and expire queued follow-ups after 24 hours.

## Suggested implementation slice

1. Probe the pinned extension SDK first: join the foreground session, register interest if required, and prove that native `user_input.requested` is observable while the TUI remains able to answer.
2. Prove Resend send and receive to the configured address, capture a real inbound fixture, and build `--simulate-inbound` at the raw parser boundary.
3. Implement the minimal daemon, authenticated pipe, token routing, and parser tests.
4. Implement away mode plus native question mirroring and compare-and-set resolution.
5. Send a root-idle completion email and inject its reply with `session.send()`.
6. Add `ask_human_by_email`, reusing the same outbound and inbound path.
7. Only if the core path is finished, spike native permission resolution and keep it disabled unless every safety gate passes.

The core demo is native question email, idle summary, and reply injection in the ordinary TUI. The explicit agent tool and permission approval reuse the same machinery but must not jeopardize that completed path.

The daemon, extension, state file, and Resend adapter are the whole product. No UI, generic MCP server, SQLite layer, webhook deployment, transcript summarizer, or retry framework is included.

### Timebox

| Time | Goal |
|---|---|
| 0:00-0:30 | Extension event-delivery probe and fallback decision |
| 0:30-1:15 | Real Resend round trip, captured fixture, parser tests |
| 1:15-2:15 | Minimal daemon, pipe authentication, token routing |
| 2:15-3:15 | Native question email and terminal/email race |
| 3:15-4:15 | Idle summary and same-session follow-up |
| 4:15-5:00 | Explicit agent tool, hardening, README, recorded demo |

Permission approval is outside the committed timebox and remains disabled unless the core path finishes early.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Plain interactive Copilot still displays and can answer a native question while `amail` is enabled.
2. With away mode armed, an emailed answer resolves that exact native request; a later terminal answer or stale email loses safely.
3. A non-aborted root idle sends one redacted summary, and a valid reply starts one visibly labeled turn in the same still-idle session.
4. Wrong sender, reused/expired token, auto-response, moved-on session, and duplicate Resend message do not inject a prompt.
5. `STOP` suppresses further delivery, and only a local command can re-arm it.
6. The same routing and parsing behavior can be demonstrated with a captured inbound fixture when live mail is delayed.

The minimum shippable submission is criteria 1-4 plus the fixture-driven demo. The explicit agent tool is the next priority; permission-by-email is optional.

## Important unknowns to validate early

- Whether `session.rpc.eventLog.registerInterest({ eventType: "user_input.requested" })` is required for a joined extension, and whether registering it preserves the native TUI prompt.
- Whether permission compare-and-set reports a race loss reliably enough for email approval.
- Whether the Resend account already has a receiving address/domain enabled.
- Whether the configured Resend account can send to the chosen recipient.
- Which inbound sender-authentication results Resend exposes.
- Which threading headers Resend preserves; this affects presentation and diagnostics, not authorization.

## Remaining implementation inputs

- The authorized recipient/sender email address.
- Whether away mode should email every root idle turn or only turns that requested human input. The current recommendation is every root idle turn while explicitly armed.

## Demo preflight

- Start the daemon explicitly with its configuration and confirm the extension can connect to its named pipe.
- Start ordinary interactive `copilot` in the repository and confirm `amail-bridge` is loaded before walking away.
- Confirm Copilot's native ask-user behavior is enabled and the extension event-delivery probe passed.
- Confirm the signed-in Resend account can send to and receive from the configured address.
- Run `amail away on`, record the local permission PIN, and confirm the extension reports the same session label.
- Use a narrow Copilot tool-permission policy; do not run the demo with blanket approval.
- Rehearse both real inbound mail and `--simulate-inbound`.
- Export the Copilot session log/transcript used for the demo so the implementation workflow can be discussed in the interview.
````

```
# GitHub Next Research Engineer: Take Home Exercise

Hi there! I'm Idan, and I'm asking you to do this little project as a prelude to our interview, so that we can talk more about how things get built and less about "describe a time when…"

The goal is for you to build a small thing that we can discuss. **You should spend 3–5 hours at most.** Our expectations are calibrated for that amount of effort.

## Instructions

Build a small tool that supports or accelerates your own engineering workflow — and make it something your coding agent can use, not just you. (Note: You should use whatever agent(s) you usually do; don't switch tools/agents just for this project.)

Form is up to you: an MCP server, a CLI, a skill, a hook, something we haven't thought of. The only real constraint is that we can run it, or watch you run it.

- ✅ **Do** finish. Done and modest beats ambitious and broken.
```

### Copilot

The top three improvements are all about making the plan finishable without sacrificing the native experience:

1. **Turn the native-event probe into a hard go/no-go milestone.** The core design still depends on an unresolved behavior: whether `user_input.requested` reaches the extension while the normal TUI remains active. Spend the first 20–30 minutes proving that exact flow. If it fails, immediately use the documented fallback: `ask_human_by_email` plus completion/reply handling. Nothing else should be built first.

2. **Collapse the committed MVP to three flows.**
   - Mirror and answer a native question by email.
   - Email the final response when the root turn becomes idle.
   - Turn a reply into one `session.send()` prompt.

   Move permission approval, durable restart recovery, multiple sessions, STOP variants, global budgets, advanced parsing, and error notifications into “follow-ups.” They are reasonable product features, but collectively contradict the 3–5 hour constraint. Native handling should remain—it is the highest-value feature to preserve.

3. **Remove the daemon/pipe architecture unless implementation proves it necessary.** A separate daemon, authenticated named pipe, HMAC handshake, atomic JSON persistence, reconnect logic, and three CLI commands are now a substantial portion of the project. For the take-home, one extension can request access to `RESEND_API_KEY`, send/poll Resend directly, and keep short-lived state in memory. A tiny local file can represent away mode. The simpler architecture is easier to finish, demonstrate, and explain; the daemon is a credible future hardening step.

+# amail: email as a Copilot control surface
+
+Status: implementation plan
+Created: 2026-09-02
+Updated: 2026-09-03
+
+## Goal
+
+`amail` lets someone step away from a standard interactive GitHub Copilot CLI session without losing the ability to:
+
+1. answer a question Copilot is waiting on;
+2. receive the result when the current turn finishes;
+3. reply with one follow-up instruction for the same session.
+
+The first version targets one local user, one interactive Copilot session, and one configured email address.
+
+## Take-home boundary
+
+The implementation must fit in 3-5 hours. The committed MVP contains exactly three flows:
+
+- **Question:** mirror a native Copilot question to email and return the answer to that exact request.
+- **Complete:** email the final response when the root turn becomes idle.
+- **Continue:** inject a reply to that completion email as the next prompt in the same session.
+
+Everything else is outside the committed MVP:
+
+- permission approval by email;
+- multiple simultaneous Copilot sessions;
+- durable recovery after Copilot or the extension exits;
+- error-specific notifications;
+- webhook deployment;
+- a separate daemon, named pipe, or database;
+- attachments, rich HTML, or a web UI;
+- generalized email commands and production security hardening.
+
+This is a version-pinned prototype for Copilot CLI `1.0.83-3`, not a production integration.
+
+## First milestone: native-event go/no-go
+
+The highest-risk assumption is whether a joined extension can observe `user_input.requested` while the standard TUI remains an active responder.
+
+Before implementing Resend or persistence:
+
+1. Load a minimal project extension and call `joinSession()`.
+2. Subscribe to `user_input.requested`.
+3. Trigger a harmless native Copilot question.
+4. If necessary, register interest through `session.rpc.eventLog.registerInterest()`.
+5. Verify that the extension receives the request **and** the terminal can still answer it.
+6. Resolve a second request through `session.rpc.ui.handlePendingUserInput()` and verify `success: true`.
+7. Answer a third request in the terminal first and verify the extension receives `success: false`.
+
+### Decision
+
+- **Probe succeeds:** native question mirroring is the MVP question flow.
+- **Probe fails or suppresses the TUI:** do not replace the native handler. Use the extension's explicit `ask_human_by_email` tool as the question flow.
+
+This decision is made in the first 30 minutes. No later work depends on an unverified native-event assumption.
+
+## User experience
+
+The user starts Copilot normally:
+
+```text
+copilot
+```
+
+The project extension joins the foreground session. Away mode is represented by a small marker file under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\amail\`; a minimal `amail away on|off` command creates or removes it.
+
+### Question
+
+When away mode is on and Copilot emits a native user-input request:
+
+```text
+Subject: [amail:7f3a] Input needed
+
+Copilot needs your input:
+
+Which pagination style should I implement?
+
+1. Previous/next links
+2. Page numbers
+3. Infinite scroll
+
+Reply with one option or its number.
+```
+
+The extension keeps the terminal prompt active. The first terminal or email answer wins through Copilot's request-ID API.
+
+If native mirroring failed its initial probe, the agent instead calls:
+
+```ts
+ask_human_by_email({
+  question: string,
+  choices?: string[]
+}): {
+  status: "answered" | "timeout",
+  answer?: string
+}
+```
+
+### Complete
+
+When the root session becomes idle without being aborted, the extension sends the last root assistant response:
+
+```text
+Subject: [amail:7f3a] Complete
+
+Repository: Qworg/amail
+
+Implemented previous/next pagination and added coverage.
+
+Reply with one follow-up instruction while this session remains idle.
+```
+
+The extension sends only while away mode is on. It ignores sub-agent idle events and labels aborted turns as interrupted rather than complete.
+
+### Continue
+
+The completion email contains a new single-use reply token. When a valid reply arrives:
+
+1. confirm the Copilot session is still the same;
+2. confirm no terminal prompt has started since the completion email;
+3. call `session.send({ prompt, mode: "enqueue", displayPrompt })`;
+4. consume the token so the instruction cannot be replayed.
+
+If the session moved on or exited, reject the reply with a short email rather than applying it to stale context.
+
+## Architecture
+
+```mermaid
+flowchart LR
+    subgraph cli["Standard interactive Copilot CLI"]
+        tui["Terminal UI"]
+        session["Foreground session"]
+        extension["amail extension"]
+        tui <--> session
+        extension <-->|"joinSession"| session
+    end
+
+    extension -->|"send and poll"| resend["Resend APIs"]
+    resend --> inbox["User inbox"]
+    inbox -->|"reply"| resend
+```
+
+The extension is the whole running application. It:
+
+- joins the foreground session;
+- observes native question, completion, and session-progress events;
+- exposes the fallback agent tool;
+- sends email and polls received messages;
+- holds pending requests and single-use tokens in memory;
+- injects accepted follow-ups with `session.send()`.
+
+There is no daemon, IPC protocol, database, or reconnect state machine in the MVP.
+
+## Configuration
+
+The extension requests `RESEND_API_KEY` through the Copilot extension environment-variable approval flow.
+
+For the exercise, the user loads only `RESEND_API_KEY` from `../.env` into the environment before starting Copilot. The extension also needs:
+
+```text
+AMAIL_TO=<authorized email address>
+AMAIL_FROM=<verified Resend sender>
+AMAIL_RECEIVE_DOMAIN=<Resend receiving domain>
+```
+
+The away marker and any captured test fixture live under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\amail\`, not in the repository.
+
+## Email routing and safety
+
+The MVP uses a deliberately small trust model:
+
+- Each outbound message gets a random, single-use 128-bit reply token.
+- Tokens are scoped to either one pending question or one follow-up prompt.
+- Only mail from the configured address is accepted.
+- Duplicate Resend message IDs and reused tokens are ignored.
+- Native answers are applied only through their original Copilot request ID.
+- A stale native answer is never converted into a new prompt.
+- Completion replies are accepted only while the recorded session is still idle.
+- Reply bodies are plain text, capped at 4 KB, with quoted history removed.
+- Auto-replies and attachments are ignored.
+- Outgoing summaries are capped and receive basic credential-pattern redaction.
+- Raw tokens and reply-to addresses are never written to the Copilot timeline.
+- Email content and routing tokens transit Resend; a compromised authorized mailbox is outside the MVP threat model.
+
+The extension does not approve tools or shell commands by email. Copilot's normal permission UI and policy remain authoritative.
+
+## In-memory state
+
+```ts
+type PendingQuestion = {
+  tokenHash: string;
+  requestId: string;
+  choices?: string[];
+  allowFreeform: boolean;
+  expiresAt: number;
+};
+
+type PendingFollowup = {
+  tokenHash: string;
+  sessionId: string;
+  idleMarker: string;
+  expiresAt: number;
+};
+```
+
+Native questions expire when:
+
+- `user_input.completed` fires;
+- the root turn aborts;
+- the extension reloads or exits;
+- the token reaches its timeout.
+
+Losing this state is acceptable: the standard terminal remains available, and stale email replies fail closed.
+
+## Timebox
+
+| Time | Work |
+|---|---|
+| 0:00-0:30 | Native-event probe and go/no-go decision |
+| 0:30-1:15 | Resend send/receive proof and captured inbound fixture |
+| 1:15-2:15 | Token routing, reply parsing, and fixture-driven tests |
+| 2:15-3:15 | Question flow: native mirroring or explicit tool fallback |
+| 3:15-4:15 | Idle completion email and same-session follow-up |
+| 4:15-5:00 | README, failure messages, cleanup, and recorded demo |
+
+If the completion/reply path is not working by 4:15, stop adding features and finish the demonstrable path.
+
+## Acceptance criteria
+
+1. Copilot remains a normal interactive TUI throughout the demo.
+2. One question can be answered by email without applying the answer to the wrong request.
+3. The terminal can still answer first, making the later email reply harmless.
+4. A non-aborted root idle sends one concise completion email.
+5. One valid reply creates one visibly labeled follow-up turn in the same idle session.
+6. Wrong sender, reused token, duplicate message, and stale-session reply do not inject a prompt.
+7. A captured inbound fixture can demonstrate routing when live mail is delayed.
+
+The minimum shippable submission is criteria 1-6. The fixture is the demo fallback, not a separate product feature.
+
+## Follow-ups deliberately deferred
+
+- native permission mirroring and approval;
+- structured elicitation;
+- batching multiple questions;
+- durable queues and restart recovery;
+- multiple connected sessions;
+- richer sender-authentication checks;
+- notification budgets, STOP commands, and operational controls;
+- a standalone daemon or hosted webhook receiver.
+
+These are reasonable next steps only after the three MVP flows prove useful.
+
+## Primary references
+
+- Copilot CLI extensions overview: https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/agents/copilot-cli/about-cli-extensions
+- Installed SDK extension guide: `C:\Users\jeffkramer\.copilot\pkg\win32-x64\1.0.83-3\copilot-sdk\docs\extensions.md`

+- Resend list received emails API: https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/emails/list-received-emails
+- Resend retrieve received email API: https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/emails/retrieve-received-email

````
# Copilot CLI Extension Examples

A practical guide to writing extensions using the `@github/copilot-sdk` extension API.

## Extension Skeleton

Every extension starts with the same boilerplate:

```js
import { joinSession } from "@github/copilot-sdk/extension";

const session = await joinSession({
    hooks: {
        /* ... */
    },
    tools: [
        /* ... */
    ],
});
```

`joinSession` returns a `CopilotSession` object you can use to send messages and subscribe to events.

> **Platform notes (Windows vs macOS/Linux):**
>
> - Use `process.platform === "win32"` to detect Windows at runtime.
> - Clipboard: `pbcopy` on macOS, `clip` on Windows.
> - Use `exec()` instead of `execFile()` for `.cmd` scripts like `code`, `npx`, `npm` on Windows.
> - PowerShell stderr redirection uses `*>&1` instead of `2>&1`.

---

## Logging to the Timeline

Use `session.log()` to surface messages to the user in the CLI timeline:

```js
const session = await joinSession({
    hooks: {
        onSessionStart: async () => {
            await session.log("My extension loaded");
        },
        onPreToolUse: async (input) => {
            if (input.toolName === "bash") {
                await session.log(`Running: ${input.toolArgs?.command}`, { ephemeral: true });
            }
        },
    },
    tools: [],
});
```

Levels: `"info"` (default), `"warning"`, `"error"`. Set `ephemeral: true` for transient messages that aren't persisted.

---

## Registering Custom Tools

Tools are functions the agent can call. Define them with a name, description, JSON Schema parameters, and a handler.

### Basic tool

```js
tools: [
    {
        name: "my_tool",
        description: "Does something useful",
        parameters: {
            type: "object",
            properties: {
                input: { type: "string", description: "The input value" },
            },
            required: ["input"],
        },
        handler: async (args) => {
            return `Processed: ${args.input}`;
        },
    },
];
```

### Tool that invokes an external shell command

```js
````

````
## Session Events

After calling `joinSession`, use `session.on()` to react to events in real time.

### Listening to a specific event type

```js
session.on("assistant.message", (event) => {
    // event.data.content has the agent's response text
});
```

### Listening to all events

```js
session.on((event) => {
    // event.type and event.data are available for all events
});
```

### Unsubscribing from events

`session.on()` returns an unsubscribe function:

```js
const unsubscribe = session.on("tool.execution_complete", (event) => {
    // event.data.success, event.data.result, event.data.error
});

// Later, stop listening
unsubscribe();
```

### Example: Auto-copy agent responses to clipboard

Combine a hook (to detect a keyword) with a session event (to capture the response):

```js
import { execFile } from "node:child_process";

let copyNextResponse = false;

function copyToClipboard(text) {
    const cmd = process.platform === "win32" ? "clip" : "pbcopy";
    const proc = execFile(cmd, [], () => {});
    proc.stdin.write(text);
    proc.stdin.end();
}

const session = await joinSession({
    hooks: {
        onUserPromptSubmitted: async (input) => {
            if (/\\bcopy\\b/i.test(input.prompt)) {
                copyNextResponse = true;
            }
        },
    },
    tools: [],
});

session.on("assistant.message", (event) => {
    if (copyNextResponse) {
        copyNextResponse = false;
        copyToClipboard(event.data.content);
    }
});
```

### Top 10 Most Useful Event Types

| Event Type                  | Description                                      | Key Data Fields                                        |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `assistant.message`         | Agent's final response                           | `content`, `messageId`, `toolRequests`                 |
| `assistant.message_delta`   | Message content chunks (ephemeral)               | `deltaContent`                                         |
| `tool.execution_start`      | A tool is about to run                           | `toolCallId`, `toolName`, `arguments`                  |
| `tool.execution_complete`   | A tool finished running                          | `toolCallId`, `success`, `result`, `error`             |
| `user.message`              | User sent a message                              | `content`, `attachments`, `source`                     |
| `session.idle`              | Session finished processing a turn               | `aborted`                                              |
| `session.error`             | An error occurred                                | `errorType`, `message`, `stack`                        |
| `permission.requested`      | Agent needs permission (shell, file write, etc.) | `requestId`, `permissionRequest.kind`                  |
| `session.shutdown`          | Session is ending                                | `shutdownType`, `totalPremiumRequests`, `codeChanges`  |
| `assistant.turn_start`      | Agent begins a new thinking/response cycle       | `turnId`                                               |

### Example: Detecting when the plan file is created or edited

Use `session.workspacePath` to locate the session's `plan.md`, then `fs.watchFile` to detect changes.
````

````
# amail milestone 1 report

Date: 2026-09-03

## Outcome

**GO:** A project extension can observe and resolve the active native Copilot question variant while preserving the standard interactive terminal responder.

The current Copilot CLI session uses `elicitation.requested`, not legacy `user_input.requested`.

## What was built

- `.github/extensions/amail-bridge/extension.mjs`
  - joins the current foreground session;
  - subscribes to both native question variants;
  - registers interest for `user_input.requested` and `elicitation.requested`;
  - records isolated probe events in the Copilot session workspace;
  - resolves opt-in elicitation probes through `session.rpc.ui.handlePendingElicitation()`.
- `scripts/verify-milestone-1.mjs`
  - parses the JSONL probe record;
  - asserts observation, extension-first resolution, and terminal-first race behavior.
- `docs/design.md`
  - records the successful milestone;
  - updates the plan to account for the active elicitation variant.

## Live tests

Probe log:

`C:\Users\jeffkramer\.copilot\session-state\a9470683-c6a8-4ceb-ba21-7f87089887e0\files\amail-milestone-1-events.jsonl`

### 1. Observe without replacing the TUI

The extension received `elicitation.requested` for request:

`8c4b7706-9bd4-4936-8933-d032fc4f2b4b`

The normal terminal form remained visible and accepted `Continue`. The extension then received the matching `elicitation.completed` event.

### 2. Extension answers first

The extension resolved request:

`5f940f9c-2ebb-4d82-941e-50113ecd8b96`

It supplied `amail-probe-auto-answer` through `handlePendingElicitation()`. The RPC returned:

```text
success: true
```

The native question completed with the extension-provided value.

### 3. Terminal answers first

The terminal resolved request:

`264dc146-c7bf-4b55-ae1e-c14b260c3b6f`

with `Continue`. Thirty seconds later, the extension attempted a conflicting answer through the same native RPC. The RPC returned:

```text
success: false
```

The terminal answer remained authoritative, demonstrating safe first-responder-wins behavior.

## Automated verification

Command:

```text
node scripts\verify-milestone-1.mjs C:\Users\jeffkramer\.copilot\session-state\a9470683-c6a8-4ceb-ba21-7f87089887e0\files\amail-milestone-1-events.jsonl
```

Result:

```text
PASS: extension observed elicitation while TUI was active
PASS: terminal completed the observed elicitation
PASS: extension resolved a native request
PASS: terminal-first answer made extension lose safely
```

Both JavaScript files also pass `node --check`.

## Conclusions

- The standard interactive Copilot experience can remain the primary responder.
- Email can be implemented as an additive responder using the native request ID.
- The runtime provides the required race protection; application-level locking is unnecessary for a single native request.
- A stale or late email answer must be discarded whenever the native RPC returns `success: false`.
- The production question flow must support the session's active native variant. On this installation that is structured elicitation.

## Remaining limitation

The legacy `user_input.requested` path is implemented in the probe but was not active in this session, so it was not live-tested. The test also proves that event-interest registration works, but it does not isolate whether registration is strictly required for elicitation delivery.
````

```
import { joinSession } from "@github/copilot-sdk/extension";
import { appendFile, mkdir } from "node:fs/promises";
import { join } from "node:path";

const session = await joinSession();
const probeDirectory = session.workspacePath
    ? join(session.workspacePath, "files")
    : join(process.env.LOCALAPPDATA ?? process.cwd(), "amail");
const probeLog = join(probeDirectory, "amail-milestone-1-events.jsonl");

await mkdir(probeDirectory, { recursive: true });

let writeQueue = Promise.resolve();

function record(type, data = {}) {
    const entry = JSON.stringify({
        timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
        sessionId: session.sessionId,
        type,
        ...data,
    });

    writeQueue = writeQueue
        .then(() => appendFile(probeLog, `${entry}\n`, "utf8"))
        .catch((error) => {
            process.stderr.write(`amail probe log error: ${error.message}\n`);
        });
}

async function answerAfterDelay(event, answer, delayMs) {
    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, delayMs));

    try {
        const result = await session.rpc.ui.handlePendingUserInput({
            requestId: event.data.requestId,
            response: {
                answer,
                wasFreeform: true,
            },
        });

        record("probe.answer_result", {
            requestId: event.data.requestId,
            answer,
            delayMs,
            success: result.success,
        });
    } catch (error) {
        record("probe.answer_error", {
            requestId: event.data.requestId,
            delayMs,
            error: error.message,
        });
    }
}

async function answerElicitationAfterDelay(event, content, delayMs) {
    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, delayMs));

    try {
        const result = await session.rpc.ui.handlePendingElicitation({
            requestId: event.data.requestId,
            result: {
                action: "accept",
                content,
            },
        });

        record("probe.elicitation_answer_result", {
            requestId: event.data.requestId,
            content,
            delayMs,
            success: result.success,
        });
    } catch (error) {
        record("probe.elicitation_answer_error", {
            requestId: event.data.requestId,
            delayMs,
            error: error.message,
        });
    }
}

session.on("user_input.requested", (event) => {
    record("user_input.requested", {
        eventId: event.id,
        requestId: event.data.requestId,
        question: event.data.question,
        choices: event.data.choices,
        allowFreeform: event.data.allowFreeform,
        agentId: event.agentId,
    });

    if (event.data.question.includes("[amail-probe:auto-answer]")) {
        void answerAfterDelay(event, "amail-probe-auto-answer", 250);
    }

    if (event.data.question.includes("[amail-probe:terminal-first]")) {
        void answerAfterDelay(event, "amail-probe-delayed-answer", 5_000);
    }
});

session.on("user_input.completed", (event) => {
    record("user_input.completed", {
        eventId: event.id,
        requestId: event.data.requestId,
        answer: event.data.answer,
        wasFreeform: event.data.wasFreeform,
        agentId: event.agentId,
    });
});

session.on("elicitation.requested", (event) => {
    record("elicitation.requested", {
        eventId: event.id,
        requestId: event.data.requestId,
        message: event.data.message,
        mode: event.data.mode,
        requestedSchema: event.data.requestedSchema,
        agentId: event.agentId,
    });

    if (event.data.message.includes("[amail-probe:auto-answer]")) {
        void answerElicitationAfterDelay(
            event,
            { response: "amail-probe-auto-answer" },
            250,
        );
    }

    if (event.data.message.includes("[amail-probe:terminal-first]")) {
        void answerElicitationAfterDelay(
            event,
            { response: "amail-probe-delayed-answer" },
            30_000,
        );
    }
});

session.on("elicitation.completed", (event) => {
    record("elicitation.completed", {
        eventId: event.id,
        requestId: event.data.requestId,
        action: event.data.action,
        content: event.data.content,
        agentId: event.agentId,
    });
});

session.on("session.shutdown", (event) => {
    record("session.shutdown", {
        eventId: event.id,
        shutdownType: event.data.shutdownType,
    });
});

const interest = await session.rpc.eventLog.registerInterest({
    eventType: "user_input.requested",
});
const elicitationInterest = await session.rpc.eventLog.registerInterest({
    eventType: "elicitation.requested",
});

record("probe.started", {
    probeLog,
    registerInterest: true,
    interestHandle: interest.handle,
    elicitationInterestHandle: elicitationInterest.handle,
});

await session.log("amail milestone 1 probe loaded (native input interest registered)");
```

````
# amail: email as a Copilot control surface

Status: implementation plan
Created: 2026-09-02
Updated: 2026-09-03

## Goal

`amail` lets someone step away from a standard interactive GitHub Copilot CLI session without losing the ability to:

1. answer a question Copilot is waiting on;
2. receive the result when the current turn finishes;
3. reply with one follow-up instruction for the same session.

The first version targets one local user, one interactive Copilot session, and one configured email address.

## Take-home boundary

The implementation must fit in 3-5 hours. The committed MVP contains exactly three flows:

- **Question:** mirror a native Copilot question to email and return the answer to that exact request.
- **Complete:** email the final response when the root turn becomes idle.
- **Continue:** inject a reply to that completion email as the next prompt in the same session.

Everything else is outside the committed MVP:

- permission approval by email;
- multiple simultaneous Copilot sessions;
- durable recovery after Copilot or the extension exits;
- error-specific notifications;
- webhook deployment;
- a separate daemon, named pipe, or database;
- attachments, rich HTML, or a web UI;
- generalized email commands and production security hardening.

This is a version-pinned prototype for Copilot CLI `1.0.83-3`, not a production integration.

## First milestone: native-event go/no-go

The highest-risk assumption is whether a joined extension can observe the session's active native question event (`user_input.requested` or `elicitation.requested`) while the standard TUI remains an active responder.

Before implementing Resend or persistence:

1. Load a minimal project extension and call `joinSession()`.
2. Subscribe to both native question event variants.
3. Trigger a harmless native Copilot question.
4. If necessary, register interest for the active event through `session.rpc.eventLog.registerInterest()`.
5. Verify that the extension receives the request **and** the terminal can still answer it.
6. Resolve a second request through the corresponding native UI RPC and verify `success: true`.
7. Answer a third request in the terminal first and verify the extension receives `success: false`.

### Decision

- **Probe succeeds:** native question mirroring is the MVP question flow.
- **Probe fails or suppresses the TUI:** do not replace the native handler. Use the extension's explicit `ask_human_by_email` tool as the question flow.

This decision is made in the first 30 minutes. No later work depends on an unverified native-event assumption.

### Milestone result

The probe passed on Copilot CLI `1.0.83-3` for the active `elicitation.requested` variant:

- registering event interest delivered the request to the extension;
- the normal structured terminal form remained usable;
- `session.rpc.ui.handlePendingElicitation()` resolved an outstanding request with `success: true`;
- after the terminal answered first, the same RPC returned `success: false`.

The extension also contains the equivalent legacy `user_input.requested` listener, but that variant was not active in this session and therefore remains unverified live.

## User experience

The user starts Copilot normally:

```text
copilot
```

The project extension joins the foreground session. Away mode is represented by a small marker file under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\amail\`; a minimal `amail away on|off` command creates or removes it.

### Question

When away mode is on and Copilot emits a native user-input request:

```text
Subject: [amail:7f3a] Input needed

Copilot needs your input:

Which pagination style should I implement?

1. Previous/next links
2. Page numbers
3. Infinite scroll

Reply with one option or its number.
```

The extension keeps the terminal prompt active. The first terminal or email answer wins through Copilot's request-ID API.

If native mirroring failed its initial probe, the agent instead calls:

```ts
ask_human_by_email({
  question: string,
  choices?: string[]
}): {
  status: "answered" | "timeout",
  answer?: string
}
```

### Complete

When the root session becomes idle without being aborted, the extension sends the last root assistant response:

```text
Subject: [amail:7f3a] Complete

Repository: Qworg/amail

Implemented previous/next pagination and added coverage.

Reply with one follow-up instruction while this session remains idle.
```

The extension sends only while away mode is on. It ignores sub-agent idle events and labels aborted turns as interrupted rather than complete.

### Continue

The completion email contains a new single-use reply token. When a valid reply arrives:

1. confirm the Copilot session is still the same;
2. confirm no terminal prompt has started since the completion email;
3. call `session.send({ prompt, mode: "enqueue", displayPrompt })`;
4. consume the token so the instruction cannot be replayed.

If the session moved on or exited, reject the reply with a short email rather than applying it to stale context.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph cli["Standard interactive Copilot CLI"]
        tui["Terminal UI"]
        session["Foreground session"]
        extension["amail extension"]
        tui <--> session
        extension <-->|"joinSession"| session
    end

    extension -->|"send and poll"| resend["Resend APIs"]
    resend --> inbox["User inbox"]
    inbox -->|"reply"| resend
```

The extension is the whole running application. It:

- joins the foreground session;
- observes native question, completion, and session-progress events;
- exposes the fallback agent tool;
- sends email and polls received messages;
- holds pending requests and single-use tokens in memory;
- injects accepted follow-ups with `session.send()`.

There is no daemon, IPC protocol, database, or reconnect state machine in the MVP.

## Configuration

The extension requests `RESEND_API_KEY` through the Copilot extension environment-variable approval flow.

For the exercise, the user loads only `RESEND_API_KEY` from `../.env` into the environment before starting Copilot. The extension also needs:

```text
AMAIL_TO=<authorized email address>
AMAIL_FROM=<verified Resend sender>
AMAIL_RECEIVE_DOMAIN=<Resend receiving domain>
```

The away marker and any captured test fixture live under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\amail\`, not in the repository.

## Email routing and safety

The MVP uses a deliberately small trust model:

- Each outbound message gets a random, single-use 128-bit reply token.
- Tokens are scoped to either one pending question or one follow-up prompt.
- Only mail from the configured address is accepted.
- Duplicate Resend message IDs and reused tokens are ignored.
- Native answers are applied only through their original Copilot request ID.
- A stale native answer is never converted into a new prompt.
- Completion replies are accepted only while the recorded session is still idle.
- Reply bodies are plain text, capped at 4 KB, with quoted history removed.
- Auto-replies and attachments are ignored.
- Outgoing summaries are capped and receive basic credential-pattern redaction.
- Raw tokens and reply-to addresses are never written to the Copilot timeline.
- Email content and routing tokens transit Resend; a compromised authorized mailbox is outside the MVP threat model.

The extension does not approve tools or shell commands by email. Copilot's normal permission UI and policy remain authoritative.

## In-memory state

```ts
type PendingQuestion = {
  tokenHash: string;
  requestId: string;
  choices?: string[];
  allowFreeform: boolean;
  expiresAt: number;
};

type PendingFollowup = {
  tokenHash: string;
  sessionId: string;
  idleMarker: string;
  expiresAt: number;
};
```

Native questions expire when:

- `user_input.completed` fires;
- the root turn aborts;
- the extension reloads or exits;
- the token reaches its timeout.

Losing this state is acceptable: the standard terminal remains available, and stale email replies fail closed.

## Timebox

| Time | Work |
|---|---|
| 0:00-0:30 | Native-event probe and go/no-go decision |
| 0:30-1:15 | Resend send/receive proof and captured inbound fixture |
| 1:15-2:15 | Token routing, reply parsing, and fixture-driven tests |
| 2:15-3:15 | Question flow: native mirroring or explicit tool fallback |
| 3:15-4:15 | Idle completion email and same-session follow-up |
| 4:15-5:00 | README, failure messages, cleanup, and recorded demo |

If the completion/reply path is not working by 4:15, stop adding features and finish the demonstrable path.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Copilot remains a normal interactive TUI throughout the demo.
2. One question can be answered by email without applying the answer to the wrong request.
3. The terminal can still answer first, making the later email reply harmless.
4. A non-aborted root idle sends one concise completion email.
5. One valid reply creates one visibly labeled follow-up turn in the same idle session.
6. Wrong sender, reused token, duplicate message, and stale-session reply do not inject a prompt.
7. A captured inbound fixture can demonstrate routing when live mail is delayed.

The minimum shippable submission is criteria 1-6. The fixture is the demo fallback, not a separate product feature.

## Follow-ups deliberately deferred

- native permission mirroring and approval;
- supporting native question variants beyond the one active in the pinned CLI session;
- batching multiple questions;
- durable queues and restart recovery;
- multiple connected sessions;
- richer sender-authentication checks;
- notification budgets, STOP commands, and operational controls;
- a standalone daemon or hosted webhook receiver.

These are reasonable next steps only after the three MVP flows prove useful.

## Primary references

- Copilot CLI extensions overview: https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/agents/copilot-cli/about-cli-extensions
- Installed SDK extension guide: `C:\Users\jeffkramer\.copilot\pkg\win32-x64\1.0.83-3\copilot-sdk\docs\extensions.md`
- Installed SDK examples: `C:\Users\jeffkramer\.copilot\pkg\win32-x64\1.0.83-3\copilot-sdk\docs\examples.md`
- Resend receiving introduction: https://resend.com/docs/dashboard/receiving/introduction
- Resend list received emails API: https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/emails/list-received-emails
- Resend retrieve received email API: https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/emails/retrieve-received-email
````

```
import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises";

const [logPath] = process.argv.slice(2);

if (!logPath) {
    process.stderr.write(
        "Usage: node scripts/verify-milestone-1.mjs <probe-log.jsonl>\n",
    );
    process.exit(2);
}

const entries = (await readFile(logPath, "utf8"))
    .split(/\r?\n/)
    .filter(Boolean)
    .map((line) => JSON.parse(line));

function find(type, predicate = () => true) {
    return entries.find((entry) => entry.type === type && predicate(entry));
}

const interestProbe = find(
    "elicitation.requested",
    (entry) => entry.message?.includes("[amail-probe:elicitation-interest]"),
);
const terminalCompletion = find(
    "elicitation.completed",
    (entry) => entry.content?.response === "Continue",
);
const extensionWin = find(
    "probe.elicitation_answer_result",
    (entry) => entry.content?.response === "amail-probe-auto-answer"
        && entry.success === true,
);
const terminalWin = find(
    "probe.elicitation_answer_result",
    (entry) => entry.content?.response === "amail-probe-delayed-answer"
        && entry.success === false,
);

const assertions = [
    ["extension observed elicitation while TUI was active", interestProbe],
    ["terminal completed the observed elicitation", terminalCompletion],
    ["extension resolved a native request", extensionWin],
    ["terminal-first answer made extension lose safely", terminalWin],
];

const failures = assertions.filter(([, value]) => !value);

for (const [description, value] of assertions) {
    process.stdout.write(`${value ? "PASS" : "FAIL"}: ${description}\n`);
}

if (failures.length > 0) {
    process.exit(1);
}
```

````
  expiresAt: number;
};
```

Native questions expire when:

- `user_input.completed` fires;
- the root turn aborts;
- the extension reloads or exits;
- the token reaches its timeout.

Losing this state is acceptable: the standard terminal remains available, and stale email replies fail closed.

## Timebox

| Time | Work |
|---|---|
| 0:00-0:30 | Native-event probe and go/no-go decision |
| 0:30-1:15 | Resend send/receive proof and captured inbound fixture |
| 1:15-2:15 | Token routing, reply parsing, and fixture-driven tests |
| 2:15-3:15 | Question flow: native mirroring or explicit tool fallback |
| 3:15-4:15 | Idle completion email and same-session follow-up |
| 4:15-5:00 | README, failure messages, cleanup, and recorded demo |

If the completion/reply path is not working by 4:15, stop adding features and finish the demonstrable path.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Copilot remains a normal interactive TUI throughout the demo.
2. One question can be answered by email without applying the answer to the wrong request.
3. The terminal can still answer first, making the later email reply harmless.
4. A non-aborted root idle sends one concise completion email.
5. One valid reply creates one visibly labeled follow-up turn in the same idle session.
6. Wrong sender, reused token, duplicate message, and stale-session reply do not inject a prompt.
7. A captured inbound fixture can demonstrate routing when live mail is delayed.

The minimum shippable submission is criteria 1-6. The fixture is the demo fallback, not a separate product feature.

## Follow-ups deliberately deferred

- native permission mirroring and approval;
- supporting native question variants beyond the one active in the pinned CLI session;
- batching multiple questions;
- durable queues and restart recovery;
- multiple connected sessions;
- richer sender-authentication checks;
- notification budgets, STOP commands, and operational controls;
- a standalone daemon or hosted webhook receiver.

These are reasonable next steps only after the three MVP flows prove useful.

- Copilot CLI extensions overview: https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/agents/copilot-cli/about-cli-extensions
````

```
import { joinSession } from "@github/copilot-sdk/extension";
import { appendFile, mkdir } from "node:fs/promises";
import { join } from "node:path";

const session = await joinSession();
const probeDirectory = session.workspacePath
    ? join(session.workspacePath, "files")
    : join(process.env.LOCALAPPDATA ?? process.cwd(), "amail");
const probeLog = join(probeDirectory, "amail-milestone-1-events.jsonl");

await mkdir(probeDirectory, { recursive: true });

let writeQueue = Promise.resolve();

function record(type, data = {}) {
    const entry = JSON.stringify({
        timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
        sessionId: session.sessionId,
        type,
        ...data,
    });

    writeQueue = writeQueue
        .then(() => appendFile(probeLog, `${entry}\n`, "utf8"))
        .catch((error) => {
            process.stderr.write(`amail probe log error: ${error.message}\n`);
        });
}

async function answerAfterDelay(event, answer, delayMs) {
    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, delayMs));

    try {
        const result = await session.rpc.ui.handlePendingUserInput({
            requestId: event.data.requestId,
            response: {
                answer,
                wasFreeform: true,
            },
        });

        record("probe.answer_result", {
            requestId: event.data.requestId,
            answer,
            delayMs,
            success: result.success,
        });
    } catch (error) {
        record("probe.answer_error", {
            requestId: event.data.requestId,
            delayMs,
            error: error.message,
        });
    }
}

async function answerElicitationAfterDelay(event, content, delayMs) {
    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, delayMs));

    try {
        const result = await session.rpc.ui.handlePendingElicitation({
            requestId: event.data.requestId,
            result: {
                action: "accept",
                content,
            },
        });

        record("probe.elicitation_answer_result", {
            requestId: event.data.requestId,
            content,
            delayMs,
            success: result.success,
        });
    } catch (error) {
        record("probe.elicitation_answer_error", {
            requestId: event.data.requestId,
            delayMs,
            error: error.message,
        });
    }
}

session.on("user_input.requested", (event) => {
    record("user_input.requested", {
        eventId: event.id,
        requestId: event.data.requestId,
        question: event.data.question,
        choices: event.data.choices,
        allowFreeform: event.data.allowFreeform,
        agentId: event.agentId,
    });

    if (event.data.question.includes("[amail-probe:auto-answer]")) {
        void answerAfterDelay(event, "amail-probe-auto-answer", 250);
    }

    if (event.data.question.includes("[amail-probe:terminal-first]")) {
        void answerAfterDelay(event, "amail-probe-delayed-answer", 5_000);
    }
});

session.on("user_input.completed", (event) => {
    record("user_input.completed", {
        eventId: event.id,
        requestId: event.data.requestId,
        answer: event.data.answer,
        wasFreeform: event.data.wasFreeform,
        agentId: event.agentId,
    });
});

session.on("elicitation.requested", (event) => {
    record("elicitation.requested", {
        eventId: event.id,
        requestId: event.data.requestId,
        message: event.data.message,
        mode: event.data.mode,
        requestedSchema: event.data.requestedSchema,
        agentId: event.agentId,
    });

    if (event.data.message.includes("[amail-probe:auto-answer]")) {
        void answerElicitationAfterDelay(
            event,
            { response: "amail-probe-auto-answer" },
            250,
        );
    }

    if (event.data.message.includes("[amail-probe:terminal-first]")) {
        void answerElicitationAfterDelay(
            event,
            { response: "amail-probe-delayed-answer" },
            30_000,
        );
    }
});

session.on("elicitation.completed", (event) => {
    record("elicitation.completed", {
        eventId: event.id,
        requestId: event.data.requestId,
        action: event.data.action,
        content: event.data.content,
        agentId: event.agentId,
    });
});

session.on("session.shutdown", (event) => {
    record("session.shutdown", {
        eventId: event.id,
        shutdownType: event.data.shutdownType,
    });
});

const interest = await session.rpc.eventLog.registerInterest({
    eventType: "user_input.requested",
});
const elicitationInterest = await session.rpc.eventLog.registerInterest({
    eventType: "elicitation.requested",
});

record("probe.started", {
    probeLog,
    registerInterest: true,
    interestHandle: interest.handle,
    elicitationInterestHandle: elicitationInterest.handle,
});

await session.log("amail milestone 1 probe loaded (native input interest registered)");
```

```
# GitHub Next Research Engineer: Take Home Exercise

Hi there! I'm Idan, and I'm asking you to do this little project as a prelude to our interview, so that we can talk more about how things get built and less about "describe a time when…"

The goal is for you to build a small thing that we can discuss. **You should spend 3–5 hours at most.** Our expectations are calibrated for that amount of effort.

## Instructions

Build a small tool that supports or accelerates your own engineering workflow — and make it something your coding agent can use, not just you. (Note: You should use whatever agent(s) you usually do; don't switch tools/agents just for this project.)

Form is up to you: an MCP server, a CLI, a skill, a hook, something we haven't thought of. The only real constraint is that we can run it, or watch you run it.

Agent-usable doesn't mean agent-only. If the right answer involves a surface a person can see or steer — a view, a review step, something you and your agent look at together — that's fair game.

Designing for an agent is a different job than designing for a person, and we're interested in how you approach that difference.

Aim for modest genuine utility. The best submissions tend to be things you actually wanted to exist before we asked.

## How you work is part of what we're discussing

Use your normal development practices, including whatever AI and agents you'd normally reach for. This is not a "coding" or algorithm design interview. Do come prepared to talk about your workflow: how you drove the work, what you verified, what you reviewed, and where you decided the quality bar was. If you have a transcript or session log from building it, bring that along — it makes for a much more concrete conversation than memory does.

## Do's and Don'ts

- ✅ **Do** finish. Done and modest beats ambitious and broken.
- ✅ **Do** cut scope aggressively — we'd rather hear why you cut something than see it half-built.
- ✅ **Do** be ready to share your screen and walk through the code.
- ✅ **You can** open-source it if you like. Though if it's polished enough to release, you probably spent too long.
- 🚫 **Do not** just wrap an API and hand the agent the raw response. That's a proxy, not an interface.
- 🚫 **Do not** let a UI eat the whole budget. If you build one, leave time to see whether it actually helps.
- 🚫 **Do not** worry about code quality or polish. Code written in a few hours looks like it, and that's fine.
- 🚫 **Do not** spend too much time on this. Seriously.

## Resources

- Model Context Protocol — https://modelcontextprotocol.io
- deps.dev — https://deps.dev
- OSV vulnerability database — https://osv.dev
```

### Copilot

I found the extension is still the milestone probe and does not import an email module, so I’ll provide a self-contained transport/parsing API with stable named exports rather than changing the extension. The implementation will use Resend’s documented `POST /emails`, `GET /emails/receiving`, and `GET /emails/receiving/:id` shapes, with typed rejection/API errors.

```
import { joinSession } from "@github/copilot-sdk/extension";
import { appendFile, mkdir } from "node:fs/promises";
import { join } from "node:path";

const session = await joinSession();
const probeDirectory = session.workspacePath
    ? join(session.workspacePath, "files")
    : join(process.env.LOCALAPPDATA ?? process.cwd(), "amail");
const probeLog = join(probeDirectory, "amail-milestone-1-events.jsonl");

await mkdir(probeDirectory, { recursive: true });

let writeQueue = Promise.resolve();

function record(type, data = {}) {
    const entry = JSON.stringify({
        timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
        sessionId: session.sessionId,
        type,
        ...data,
    });

    writeQueue = writeQueue
        .then(() => appendFile(probeLog, `${entry}\n`, "utf8"))
        .catch((error) => {
            process.stderr.write(`amail probe log error: ${error.message}\n`);
        });
}

async function answerAfterDelay(event, answer, delayMs) {
    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, delayMs));

    try {
        const result = await session.rpc.ui.handlePendingUserInput({
            requestId: event.data.requestId,
            response: {
                answer,
                wasFreeform: true,
            },
        });

        record("probe.answer_result", {
            requestId: event.data.requestId,
            answer,
            delayMs,
            success: result.success,
        });
    } catch (error) {
        record("probe.answer_error", {
            requestId: event.data.requestId,
            delayMs,
            error: error.message,
        });
    }
}

async function answerElicitationAfterDelay(event, content, delayMs) {
    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, delayMs));

    try {
        const result = await session.rpc.ui.handlePendingElicitation({
            requestId: event.data.requestId,
            result: {
                action: "accept",
                content,
            },
        });

        record("probe.elicitation_answer_result", {
            requestId: event.data.requestId,
            content,
            delayMs,
            success: result.success,
        });
    } catch (error) {
        record("probe.elicitation_answer_error", {
            requestId: event.data.requestId,
            delayMs,
            error: error.message,
        });
    }
}

session.on("user_input.requested", (event) => {
    record("user_input.requested", {
        eventId: event.id,
        requestId: event.data.requestId,
        question: event.data.question,
        choices: event.data.choices,
        allowFreeform: event.data.allowFreeform,
        agentId: event.agentId,
    });

    if (event.data.question.includes("[amail-probe:auto-answer]")) {
        void answerAfterDelay(event, "amail-probe-auto-answer", 250);
    }

    if (event.data.question.includes("[amail-probe:terminal-first]")) {
        void answerAfterDelay(event, "amail-probe-delayed-answer", 5_000);
    }
});

session.on("user_input.completed", (event) => {
    record("user_input.completed", {
        eventId: event.id,
        requestId: event.data.requestId,
        answer: event.data.answer,
        wasFreeform: event.data.wasFreeform,
        agentId: event.agentId,
    });
});

session.on("elicitation.requested", (event) => {
    record("elicitation.requested", {
        eventId: event.id,
        requestId: event.data.requestId,
        message: event.data.message,
        mode: event.data.mode,
        requestedSchema: event.data.requestedSchema,
        agentId: event.agentId,
    });

    if (event.data.message.includes("[amail-probe:auto-answer]")) {
        void answerElicitationAfterDelay(
            event,
            { response: "amail-probe-auto-answer" },
            250,
        );
    }

    if (event.data.message.includes("[amail-probe:terminal-first]")) {
        void answerElicitationAfterDelay(
            event,
            { response: "amail-probe-delayed-answer" },
            30_000,
        );
    }
});

session.on("elicitation.completed", (event) => {
    record("elicitation.completed", {
        eventId: event.id,
        requestId: event.data.requestId,
        action: event.data.action,
        content: event.data.content,
        agentId: event.agentId,
    });
});

session.on("session.shutdown", (event) => {
    record("session.shutdown", {
        eventId: event.id,
        shutdownType: event.data.shutdownType,
    });
});

const interest = await session.rpc.eventLog.registerInterest({
    eventType: "user_input.requested",
});
const elicitationInterest = await session.rpc.eventLog.registerInterest({
    eventType: "elicitation.requested",
});

record("probe.started", {
    probeLog,
```
